meta.source: Evaluate-Compete outcomes (SERC at Carleton College), the 18 skills the MATE ROV Competition marks with icons
meta.scope_note: All 18 outcome categories: nine general (employability) and nine specific to the MATE ROV Competition. The MATE manuals show them as icons in their Overview and say the icons mark which competition requirements help develop each skill. This catalog uses Evaluate-Compete's own names; where the manual's icon label differs the label is recorded as icon_label. Each skill also carries its 'components' (48 in all), the outcome components Evaluate-Compete lists under it, read 2026-11-20 from the page revised November 25, 2024; each is paraphrased here with a letter code and a very short phrase. The page numbers none of them and does not say how they are measured. One component under Ability to Deal with Obstacles repeats one under Autonomy in the source; both are kept.
meta.codes_note: Codes are this project's: EMP.1 to EMP.9 (employability) and ROV.1 to ROV.9, in the order Evaluate-Compete lists them, with a letter for each of a skill's components (EMP.3b, ROV.7d). They are not MATE's or Evaluate-Compete's.
meta.license_note: The skill names are quoted as labels; every description and component is a paraphrase written for this project, not the page's text. The page is offered under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is cited.

items.name: Communication
items.paraphrase: Explains the engineering process and the design to a broad audience, uses images, diagrams and data well, and writes clearly.

components.text: Explain the engineering process and the design to any audience
Use images, diagrams and data to show a design or process
Write clearly and correctly

items.name: Creativity
items.paraphrase: Looks at a problem from several angles, connects ideas and applies knowledge in new ways.

components.text: Come at a problem from different angles
Connect several ideas or approaches
Apply what you know in new ways

items.name: Entrepreneurship
items.paraphrase: Builds a product or service that meets customer needs, understands operations and budgets, and manages a project.

components.text: Make a product or service that meets a customer's need
Understand how a business runs and what it costs
Manage a project

items.name: Autonomy
items.paraphrase: Works independently, knows when to ask for help, takes criticism well, and tries again after failing.

components.text: Work on your own and know when to ask for help
Take criticism and use the feedback
Take risks and try again after failing

items.name: Ability to Deal with Obstacles
items.paraphrase: Keeps going after setbacks, stays flexible and improvises a fix for a design or equipment problem.

components.text: Keep going through setbacks and surprises
Stay flexible and willing to try again (the source repeats Autonomy here)
Improvise a quick fix to a design or equipment problem

items.name: Intellectual Development
items.paraphrase: Sees that problems are more complex than they first look, accepts that more than one design can be acceptable, and knows the limits of what they know.

components.text: See that problems are more complicated than they look
Accept that more than one design can work
Know the limits of what you know

items.name: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving
items.paraphrase: Stays open-minded but skeptical about solutions, looks for root causes and compares alternative designs or ways of operating.

components.text: Stay open-minded but skeptical about possible solutions
Find the root cause of a problem and the right fix
Evaluate alternative designs or ways of operating

items.name: Project Knowledge and Skills
items.paraphrase: Understands the engineering and science behind the vehicle and its operation, and has the skills to do the work.

components.text: Understand the engineering and science behind the vehicle and how it runs
Have the skills to design and run the vehicle
Master the skills it takes to compete well

items.name: Teamwork/Collaboration
items.paraphrase: Treats others with respect, works well in a team and shares knowledge within and across teams.

components.text: Be collegial and treat others with respect
Work effectively in a team
Share knowledge in your team and with other teams

items.name: Vehicle Design, Buoyancy, Propulsion
items.paraphrase: Applies buoyancy and ballast principles, the properties of water and the physics of propulsion to the vehicle's design.

components.text: Apply buoyancy and ballast to the vehicle's design
Apply the properties of water, such as pressure rising with depth
Apply hydrodynamics and Newton's laws to propulsion

items.name: Systems Design
items.paraphrase: Understands the engineering principles behind the vehicle's systems and applies them to designing those systems.

components.text: Apply engineering principles to designing the vehicle's systems

items.name: Structure
items.paraphrase: Can explain the trade-offs and reasoning behind the vehicle's cost, size and weight.

components.text: Explain the trade-offs behind cost, size and weight

items.name: Control/Electrical
items.paraphrase: Applies electrical concepts to the control and electrical systems and integrates software and electronics into vehicle control.

components.text: Apply electrical concepts to the control and power system
Integrate software and electronics into vehicle control

items.name: Sensors/Payload/Tools
items.paraphrase: Can identify and evaluate sensors and tooling, cameras included, against the mission's needs, and applies programming to control and sensing.

components.text: Choose and evaluate sensors, tools and cameras for the mission
Program the control and sensing

items.name: Safety
items.paraphrase: Understands safety principles and applies them to people, equipment and operations.

components.text: Apply safety principles to people, equipment and operations

items.name: Project Management
items.paraphrase: Organizes the team as a company with defined roles, plans the deliverables, tracks a budget, and manages tasks and time.

components.text: Organize as a company with a role for everyone
Plan and stay on task through every deliverable
Create and track a budget
Manage tasks and time

items.name: Technical Presentation
items.paraphrase: Produces detailed documentation, presents it to support the design, builds a display that explains the design, and can explain its strengths and weaknesses.

components.text: Write detailed documentation
Present the documentation to support the design
Make a marketing display that explains the design
Explain the design's strengths and weaknesses

items.name: Technology and Society
items.paraphrase: Connects the theme and mission tasks to real-world problems and is aware of environmental, social and governance factors in business decisions.

components.text: Relate the competition theme to real-world issues
Relate the mission tasks to real technical problems
Know how organizations weigh environmental, social and governance factors
